title: A Context-Integrated Transformer-Based Neural Network for Auction Design

en.text: Auction design is one of the oldest and most stubborn problems in computational economics. The goal sounds simple: write down a set of rules that maximizes the seller's expected revenue while staying incentive-compatible, so that no bidder can gain by misreporting what an item is worth to them. Myerson settled the single-item case in 1981. But the moment you move to multiple items, the optimal auction is still not understood four decades later, even for just two bidders and two items.

Deep learning has recently offered a fresh angle: treat the auction mechanism itself as a neural network and train it, from data, to maximize revenue subject to a zero-regret constraint. The catch is that existing neural auction designers such as RegretNet and EquivariantNet come with a hard limitation. They either handle only a fixed number of bidders and items, or they assume the auction is symmetric. Real markets break both assumptions: in e-commerce advertising the number of bidders and ad slots changes from round to round, bidders and items each carry rich public features, and the revenue-optimal mechanism is often asymmetric.

This ICML 2022 paper introduces CITransNet (Context-Integrated Transformer Network), which treats the public context of bidders and items as a first-class input. Built on a transformer, it is naturally permutation-equivariant over both bidders and items, it can represent asymmetric mechanisms, and, crucially, its parameter count does not depend on the auction's size. A model trained at one scale can be applied directly to auctions larger or smaller than any it saw during training.

en.caption: Figure 1. The CITransNet architecture. The network takes a bidding matrix b, bidder-contexts x, and item-contexts y; it embeds the contexts and assembles them with the bids into an initial per-bidder-item representation E, passes this through one or more transformer-based interaction layers that model the mutual influence among bidders and items, and reads out the allocation g and payments p in a final output layer. Each interaction layer sums three views of the data (a global average, a transformer applied along each column, and a transformer applied along each row), which captures rich interactions while keeping the mechanism permutation-equivariant.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12489
Code: https://github.com/zjduan/CITransNet
Why context and variable size matter

Classical automated auction design treats each auction as an isolated numerical problem: given a set of bidders' valuations over a set of items, output an allocation and payments. But in real ad auctions, bidders and items are not anonymous. User profiles, advertiser verticals, and product categories are public features that strongly shape what a good mechanism looks like, and ignoring them throws away usable information. At the same time, the number of bidders and slots shifts every round, so a designer whose network is hard-wired to one fixed scale is awkward to deploy. CITransNet targets both problems at once: ingest the context, and accept variable-length input.
How CITransNet is built

CITransNet builds on the RegretNet learning framework and casts "design the optimal auction" as a constrained optimization: among all mechanisms that satisfy individual rationality (IR), minimize the negative expected payment (that is, maximize revenue) while driving each bidder's expected regret (the largest extra utility they could gain by misreporting) to zero. IR is guaranteed by the architecture; the zero-regret condition is approached as a soft constraint during training, using RegretNet's augmented-Lagrangian method. For this contextual setting the paper also proves a sample-complexity bound, showing that a mechanism trained on finitely many samples generalizes with controlled error.

The heart of the network is its interaction layer. As Figure 1 shows, the bidder-contexts x and item-contexts y are first embedded into vectors and concatenated with the bids b into a three-dimensional bidder-by-item-by-feature tensor. That tensor then flows through one or more transformer-based interaction layers, and each layer adds three views of the data: a global average over everything, a transformer run down each column (all bidders for a given item), and a transformer run across each row (all items for a given bidder). This lets the model capture the complex give-and-take among bidders and items while staying equivariant to their ordering: swap two bidders at the input and the output simply swaps to match, rather than changing the mechanism. Because none of the parameters are tied to a specific bidder or item count, the same network handles auctions of different sizes.
Experiments: recover the known optimum, then beat strong baselines

The authors evaluate on nine synthetic contextual-auction settings. Settings A–C are single-item auctions whose optimal mechanism follows analytically from Myerson's 1981 theory and serve as a sanity check; Settings D–I are multi-item auctions up to 5 bidders × 10 items (to the authors' knowledge the largest auction size studied in the deep auction-design literature) with either discrete contexts or continuous ten-dimensional context vectors. Every number is averaged over five runs.

On the single-item settings, CITransNet essentially reproduces the Myerson optimum: in Setting A it earns revenue 0.593 against the analytical optimum of 0.594, with regret below 0.001. Tellingly, the context-free RegretNet and EquivariantNet fall short of the optimum even here, which shows that integrating context is not a nicety but a necessity.

The real test is the multi-item settings, where no analytical solution exists and the only yardstick is a strong baseline. Table 1 compares revenue on three representative settings: E (3×10, discrete), F (5×10, discrete, the largest), and G (2×5, continuous context). Item-wise Myerson applies the single-item Myerson auction independently to each item; CIRegretNet and CIEquivariantNet replace CITransNet's transformer interaction layers with RegretNet's fully-connected layers and EquivariantNet's equivariant layers respectively, while still receiving context.

en.caption: Table 1. Revenue on three representative multi-item settings (higher is better; regret ≤0.003 in all settings). CITransNet achieves the highest revenue in all six multi-item settings; three are shown here. Its margin over Item-wise Myerson reaches about 5.6% on Setting E and about 9.9% on the continuous-context Setting G.

en.text: CITransNet wins on all six multi-item settings; the three above are representative. It consistently beats the strong Item-wise Myerson baseline, and it also beats CIRegretNet and CIEquivariantNet, which receive the same context. Since the only thing separating those three models is the interaction-layer architecture, the comparison pins the gain squarely on the transformer interaction layers.
Train at one scale, transfer to another

Because CITransNet's parameter count is independent of auction size, it gains an unusual ability: train at one scale and evaluate at another, which the authors call out-of-setting generalization. Figure 2 shows three such experiments. A model trained on one setting is run on auctions with a different number of bidders or items, and compared against the Item-wise Myerson baseline.

en.caption: Figure 2. Out-of-setting generalization. A model trained at a fixed scale is evaluated on the same kind of auction with a different number of bidders or items; regret stays below 0.001 throughout. (a) Trained on Setting E (3×10, discrete), evaluated across bidder counts; (b) trained on Setting D (2×5, discrete), evaluated across item counts; (c) trained on Setting G (2×5, continuous), evaluated across item counts. The CITransNet curve (blue) stays above the baseline (red) across most unseen sizes.

en.text: Even when faced with bidder or item counts it never saw in training, CITransNet keeps regret low and outperforms the baseline on most unseen sizes. For an online system that constantly juggles a changing number of participants, this train-once, run-across-scales property is genuinely practical.
Takeaway and limits

The core message is compact: treat public context as a first-class input and process it with a permutation-equivariant transformer, and you can learn auction mechanisms that are near-optimal, asymmetric when they need to be, and incentive-compatible. Because the network's size is independent of the number of bidders and items, one trained model transfers to auction sizes it never saw. The honest caveats: these results are on synthetic data up to a 5×10 scale, zero regret is approached as a soft constraint rather than strictly guaranteed, and there is still distance to a production-scale industrial ad system. Still, as the first architecture to unite contextual features, asymmetric mechanisms, and out-of-setting generalization, CITransNet points a practical direction for learning auctions with neural networks.

zh.text: 拍卖设计是计算经济学里最经典、也最顽固的问题之一。目标听上去很朴素：写下一套规则，让卖方的期望收益最大，同时保证「激励相容」（incentive compatibility），即如实报价对每个参与者都是最优选择，没人有动机撒谎。单物品的情形早在 1981 年就被 Myerson 解决，但一旦进入多物品场景，即便只有两个买家、两件商品，最优拍卖机制在四十多年后依然没有解析答案。

近年来深度学习给这个老问题带来了新思路：把拍卖机制本身当成一个神经网络，用数据训练它，在「零后悔」（zero regret）的约束下最大化收益。但已有的神经拍卖设计器，如 RegretNet 和 EquivariantNet，都带着一条硬约束——要么只能处理固定数量的买家和物品，要么强行假设拍卖是对称的。真实市场恰恰两条都不满足：在电商广告竞价里，每一轮的参与者数量都在变，买家和物品各自带着丰富的公开特征（context），而收益最优的机制往往是不对称的。

这篇发表于 ICML 2022 的工作提出 CITransNet（Context-Integrated Transformer Network），把买家和物品的公开上下文当作「一等输入」直接喂给网络。它以 Transformer 为骨架，天然对买家和物品保持置换等变（permutation-equivariant），既能表达不对称机制，参数量又与拍卖规模无关——这意味着在一个规模上训练好的模型，可以直接用于它从未见过的、更大或更小的拍卖。

zh.caption: 图1 CITransNet 的整体结构。网络接收竞价矩阵 b、买家上下文 x 和物品上下文 y，先把上下文嵌入并与竞价拼成每个「买家-物品」对的初始表示 E，再经过一层或多层 Transformer 交互层建模买家与物品间的相互影响，最后由输出层给出分配 g 和支付 p。每个交互层同时融合三种视角——全局平均、按列的 Transformer 和按行的 Transformer——从而在保持置换等变的同时捕捉复杂的交互关系。

zh.text: 论文地址：https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12489
开源代码：https://github.com/zjduan/CITransNet
为什么「上下文」和「变长输入」这么关键

传统的自动拍卖设计把每一场拍卖看成孤立的数值问题：给定若干买家对若干物品的估值，输出分配和支付。但在真实的广告竞价里，买家和物品都不是匿名的——用户画像、广告主行业、商品类目这些公开特征会显著影响什么才算好机制，忽略它们等于把一份本可利用的信息扔掉。与此同时，每一轮竞价的买家数和广告位数都在变，一个把网络结构绑死在某个固定规模上的设计器，在实际系统里很难部署。CITransNet 想同时解决这两件事：吃进上下文，并接受变长的输入。
CITransNet 是怎么构造的

CITransNet 建立在 RegretNet 的学习框架之上，把「设计最优拍卖」写成一个约束优化问题：在所有满足个体理性（IR）的机制中，最小化负的期望支付（即最大化收益），同时把每个买家的期望「后悔」（regret，即谎报能带来的最大额外效用）约束为零。个体理性由网络结构直接保证，零后悔则借用 RegretNet 的增广拉格朗日方法，在训练中作为软约束逐步逼近。针对这个上下文版本，论文还证明了一个样本复杂度上界，说明用有限样本训练出的机制，其泛化误差是可控的。

网络的核心是「交互层」。如图1所示，买家上下文 x 和物品上下文 y 先被嵌入成向量，再和竞价 b 拼接成一个「买家 × 物品 × 特征」的三维张量。这个张量随后流过一层或多层 Transformer 交互层，每一层把数据的三种视角相加：一个对全体求平均的全局视角，一个沿「每一列」（同一物品下的所有买家）运行的 Transformer，以及一个沿「每一行」（同一买家下的所有物品）运行的 Transformer。这样的设计让模型既能捕捉买家与物品之间复杂的相互影响，又对买家和物品的排列顺序保持等变——交换两个买家的输入，输出也只是相应交换，机制本身不变。正因为参数不绑定到具体的买家数或物品数，同一个网络可以处理不同规模的拍卖。
实验：先复现已知最优，再赢过强基线
论文在九个合成的上下文拍卖设定上做了评测。其中设定 A–C 是单物品拍卖，最优机制可由 Myerson 1981 年的理论解析给出，用来做「体检」；设定 D–I 是多物品拍卖，规模最大到 5 个买家 × 10 件物品（据作者所知，这是深度拍卖设计文献里考察过的最大规模），上下文既有离散的，也有连续的十维向量。所有数字都是 5 次运行的平均。
在单物品设定上，CITransNet 几乎精确复现了 Myerson 最优：以设定 A 为例，它拿到 0.593 的收益，对应的理论最优是 0.594，后悔值低于 0.001。值得注意的是，不带上下文的 RegretNet 和 EquivariantNet 在这些简单设定上都够不到最优，这直接说明「把上下文整合进来」不是锦上添花，而是必要的。

真正的看点在多物品设定上——这里没有解析解，只能和强基线比。下表对比了几种方法在三个代表性设定上的收益：E（3×10，离散）、F（5×10，离散，最大规模）和 G（2×5，连续上下文）。Item-wise Myerson 是把 Myerson 单物品拍卖逐个物品独立应用得到的强基线；CIRegretNet 和 CIEquivariantNet 则是把 CITransNet 的 Transformer 交互层分别换成 RegretNet 的全连接层和 EquivariantNet 的等变层，但同样吃上下文。

zh.caption: 表1 三个代表性多物品设定下的收益对比（数值越高越好；所有设定中后悔均 ≤0.003）。CITransNet 在全部六个多物品设定中都取得最高收益，此处展示其中三个；在设定 E 上比 Item-wise Myerson 高约 5.6%，在连续上下文的设定 G 上领先约 9.9%。

zh.text: CITransNet 在全部六个多物品设定里都拿到了最高收益，表1里的三个只是代表。它不仅稳定超过 Item-wise Myerson 这个强基线，也超过了同样带上下文的 CIRegretNet 和 CIEquivariantNet。由于这三者唯一的区别就是交互层的结构，这个对比把性能提升干净地归因到了 Transformer 交互层本身。
训练一个规模，迁移到另一个规模
CITransNet 参数量与拍卖规模无关这一性质，带来一个有意思的能力：在某个规模上训练，直接在另一个规模上评测，作者称之为「out-of-setting 泛化」。图2展示了三组这样的实验：把在某个设定上训练好的模型，分别放到买家数或物品数不同的拍卖上运行，并和 Item-wise Myerson 基线比较收益。

zh.caption: 图2 Out-of-setting 泛化结果。模型在一个固定规模上训练，再在买家数或物品数不同的同类拍卖上评测，所有实验的后悔均低于 0.001。(a) 在设定 E（3×10 离散）上训练，评测不同买家数；(b) 在设定 D（2×5 离散）上训练，评测不同物品数；(c) 在设定 G（2×5 连续）上训练，评测不同物品数。蓝线（CITransNet）在大部分未见规模上都稳定高于红线（基线）。

zh.text: 可以看到，即便面对训练时从未出现过的买家数或物品数，CITransNet 依然保持低后悔，并在大多数未见规模上超过基线。对一个需要频繁应对不同参与者数量的线上系统来说，这种「训一次、跨规模用」的性质相当实用。
一句话总结与边界

CITransNet 的核心信息很简单：把公开上下文当作一等输入，用一个置换等变的 Transformer 去处理，就能学出接近最优、必要时不对称、且激励相容的拍卖机制；又因为网络规模与买家数、物品数无关，一个训练好的模型可以迁移到未见过的拍卖规模上。需要留意的是，这些结论都建立在合成数据、最大 5×10 的规模上，零后悔是作为软约束逼近而非严格保证，离真实工业级广告系统仍有距离。但作为把上下文特征、不对称机制和跨规模泛化三者统一到一个架构里的尝试，它给「用神经网络设计拍卖」这条路指出了一个务实的方向。

近年来深度学习给这个老问题带来了新思路：把拍卖机制本身当成一个神经网络，用数据训练它，在「零后悔」（zero regret）的约束下最大化收益。但已有的神经拍卖设计器，如 RegretNet 和 EquivariantNet，都带着一条硬约束——要么只能处理固定数量的买家和物品，要么强行假设拍卖是对称的。真实市场恰恰两条都不满足：在电商广告竞价里，每一轮的参与者数量都在变，买家和物品各自带着丰富的公开特征（context），而收益最优的机制往往是不对称的。

这篇发表于 ICML 2022 的工作提出 CITransNet（Context-Integrated Transformer Network），把买家和物品的公开上下文当作「一等输入」直接喂给网络。它以 Transformer 为骨架，天然对买家和物品保持置换等变（permutation-equivariant），既能表达不对称机制，参数量又与拍卖规模无关——这意味着在一个规模上训练好的模型，可以直接用于它从未见过的、更大或更小的拍卖。

zh.title: ICML 2022 | 把「上下文」交给 Transformer，让神经网络学出更好的拍卖机制
zh.subtitle: 北京大学与 Google 提出 CITransNet：一个置换等变、可处理变长输入的上下文拍卖设计网络

en.caption: Figure 1. The CITransNet architecture. The network takes a bidding matrix b, bidder-contexts x, and item-contexts y; it embeds the contexts and assembles them with the bids into an initial per-bidder-item representation E, passes this through one or more transformer-based interaction layers that model the mutual influence among bidders and items, and reads out the allocation g and payments p in a final output layer. Each interaction layer sums three views of the data (a global average, a transformer applied along each column, and a transformer applied along each row), which captures rich interactions while keeping the mechanism permutation-equivariant.

en.text: How CITransNet is built

CITransNet builds on the RegretNet learning framework and casts "design the optimal auction" as a constrained optimization: among all mechanisms that satisfy individual rationality (IR), minimize the negative expected payment (that is, maximize revenue) while driving each bidder's expected regret (the largest extra utility they could gain by misreporting) to zero. IR is guaranteed by the architecture; the zero-regret condition is approached as a soft constraint during training, using RegretNet's augmented-Lagrangian method. For this contextual setting the paper also proves a sample-complexity bound, showing that a mechanism trained on finitely many samples generalizes with controlled error.

The heart of the network is its interaction layer. As Figure 1 shows, the bidder-contexts x and item-contexts y are first embedded into vectors and concatenated with the bids b into a three-dimensional bidder-by-item-by-feature tensor. That tensor then flows through one or more transformer-based interaction layers, and each layer adds three views of the data: a global average over everything, a transformer run down each column (all bidders for a given item), and a transformer run across each row (all items for a given bidder). This lets the model capture the complex give-and-take among bidders and items while staying equivariant to their ordering: swap two bidders at the input and the output simply swaps to match, rather than changing the mechanism. Because none of the parameters are tied to a specific bidder or item count, the same network handles auctions of different sizes.

zh.caption: 图1 CITransNet 的整体结构。网络接收竞价矩阵 b、买家上下文 x 和物品上下文 y，先把上下文嵌入并与竞价拼成每个「买家-物品」对的初始表示 E，再经过一层或多层 Transformer 交互层建模买家与物品间的相互影响，最后由输出层给出分配 g 和支付 p。每个交互层同时融合三种视角——全局平均、按列的 Transformer 和按行的 Transformer——从而在保持置换等变的同时捕捉复杂的交互关系。

zh.text: CITransNet 是怎么构造的

CITransNet 建立在 RegretNet 的学习框架之上，把「设计最优拍卖」写成一个约束优化问题：在所有满足个体理性（IR）的机制中，最小化负的期望支付（即最大化收益），同时把每个买家的期望「后悔」（regret，即谎报能带来的最大额外效用）约束为零。个体理性由网络结构直接保证，零后悔则借用 RegretNet 的增广拉格朗日方法，在训练中作为软约束逐步逼近。针对这个上下文版本，论文还证明了一个样本复杂度上界，说明用有限样本训练出的机制，其泛化误差是可控的。

网络的核心是「交互层」。如图1所示，买家上下文 x 和物品上下文 y 先被嵌入成向量，再和竞价 b 拼接成一个「买家 × 物品 × 特征」的三维张量。这个张量随后流过一层或多层 Transformer 交互层，每一层把数据的三种视角相加：一个对全体求平均的全局视角，一个沿「每一列」（同一物品下的所有买家）运行的 Transformer，以及一个沿「每一行」（同一买家下的所有物品）运行的 Transformer。这样的设计让模型既能捕捉买家与物品之间复杂的相互影响，又对买家和物品的排列顺序保持等变——交换两个买家的输入，输出也只是相应交换，机制本身不变。正因为参数不绑定到具体的买家数或物品数，同一个网络可以处理不同规模的拍卖。

Every number is averaged over five runs.

On the single-item settings, CITransNet essentially reproduces the Myerson optimum: in Setting A it earns revenue 0.593 against the analytical optimum of 0.594, with regret below 0.001. Tellingly, the context-free RegretNet and EquivariantNet fall short of the optimum even here, which shows that integrating context is not a nicety but a necessity.

The real test is the multi-item settings, where no analytical solution exists and the only yardstick is a strong baseline. Table 1 compares revenue on three representative settings: E (3×10, discrete), F (5×10, discrete, the largest), and G (2×5, continuous context). Item-wise Myerson applies the single-item Myerson auction independently to each item; CIRegretNet and CIEquivariantNet replace CITransNet's transformer interaction layers with RegretNet's fully-connected layers and EquivariantNet's equivariant layers respectively, while still receiving context.

en.caption: Table 1. Revenue on three representative multi-item settings (higher is better; regret ≤0.003 in all settings). CITransNet achieves the highest revenue in all six multi-item settings; three are shown here. Its margin over Item-wise Myerson reaches about 5.6% on Setting E and about 9.9% on the continuous-context Setting G.

en.text: CITransNet wins on all six multi-item settings; the three above are representative. It consistently beats the strong Item-wise Myerson baseline, and it also beats CIRegretNet and CIEquivariantNet, which receive the same context. Since the only thing separating those three models is the interaction-layer architecture, the comparison pins the gain squarely on the transformer interaction layers.

en.text: Train at one scale, transfer to another

Because CITransNet's parameter count is independent of auction size, it gains an unusual ability: train at one scale and evaluate at another, which the authors call out-of-setting generalization. Figure 2 shows three such experiments. A model trained on one setting is run on auctions with a different number of bidders or items, and compared against the Item-wise Myerson baseline.

en.caption: Figure 2. Out-of-setting generalization. A model trained at a fixed scale is evaluated on the same kind of auction with a different number of bidders or items; regret stays below 0.001 throughout. (a) Trained on Setting E (3×10, discrete), evaluated across bidder counts; (b) trained on Setting D (2×5, discrete), evaluated across item counts; (c) trained on Setting G (2×5, continuous), evaluated across item counts. The CITransNet curve (blue) stays above the baseline (red) across most unseen sizes.

en.text: Even when faced with bidder or item counts it never saw in training, CITransNet keeps regret low and outperforms the baseline on most unseen sizes. For an online system that constantly juggles a changing number of participants, this train-once, run-across-scales property is genuinely practical.

zh.text: 训练一个规模，迁移到另一个规模
CITransNet 参数量与拍卖规模无关这一性质，带来一个有意思的能力：在某个规模上训练，直接在另一个规模上评测，作者称之为「out-of-setting 泛化」。图2展示了三组这样的实验：把在某个设定上训练好的模型，分别放到买家数或物品数不同的拍卖上运行，并和 Item-wise Myerson 基线比较收益。

zh.caption: 图2 Out-of-setting 泛化结果。模型在一个固定规模上训练，再在买家数或物品数不同的同类拍卖上评测，所有实验的后悔均低于 0.001。(a) 在设定 E（3×10 离散）上训练，评测不同买家数；(b) 在设定 D（2×5 离散）上训练，评测不同物品数；(c) 在设定 G（2×5 连续）上训练，评测不同物品数。蓝线（CITransNet）在大部分未见规模上都稳定高于红线（基线）。

zh.text: 可以看到，即便面对训练时从未出现过的买家数或物品数，CITransNet 依然保持低后悔，并在大多数未见规模上超过基线。对一个需要频繁应对不同参与者数量的线上系统来说，这种「训一次、跨规模用」的性质相当实用。

en.text: Auction design is one of the oldest and most stubborn problems in computational economics. The goal sounds simple: write down a set of rules that maximizes the seller's expected revenue while staying incentive-compatible, so that no bidder can gain by misreporting what an item is worth to them. Myerson settled the single-item case in 1981. But the moment you move to multiple items, the optimal auction is still not understood four decades later, even for just two bidders and two items.

Deep learning has recently offered a fresh angle: treat the auction mechanism itself as a neural network and train it, from data, to maximize revenue subject to a zero-regret constraint. The catch is that existing neural auction designers such as RegretNet and EquivariantNet come with a hard limitation. They either handle only a fixed number of bidders and items, or they assume the auction is symmetric. Real markets break both assumptions: in e-commerce advertising the number of bidders and ad slots changes from round to round, bidders and items each carry rich public features, and the revenue-optimal mechanism is often asymmetric.

This ICML 2022 paper introduces CITransNet (Context-Integrated Transformer Network), which treats the public context of bidders and items as a first-class input. Built on a transformer, it is naturally permutation-equivariant over both bidders and items, it can represent asymmetric mechanisms, and, crucially, its parameter count does not depend on the auction's size. A model trained at one scale can be applied directly to auctions larger or smaller than any it saw during training.

近年来深度学习给这个老问题带来了新思路：把拍卖机制本身当成一个神经网络，用数据训练它，在「零后悔」（zero regret）的约束下最大化收益。但已有的神经拍卖设计器，如 RegretNet 和 EquivariantNet，都带着一条硬约束——要么只能处理固定数量的买家和物品，要么强行假设拍卖是对称的。真实市场恰恰两条都不满足：在电商广告竞价里，每一轮的参与者数量都在变，买家和物品各自带着丰富的公开特征（context），而收益最优的机制往往是不对称的。

这篇发表于 ICML 2022 的工作提出 CITransNet（Context-Integrated Transformer Network），把买家和物品的公开上下文当作「一等输入」直接喂给网络。它以 Transformer 为骨架，天然对买家和物品保持置换等变（permutation-equivariant），既能表达不对称机制，参数量又与拍卖规模无关——这意味着在一个规模上训练好的模型，可以直接用于它从未见过的、更大或更小的拍卖。

zh.caption: 图1 CITransNet 的整体结构。网络接收竞价矩阵 b、买家上下文 x 和物品上下文 y，先把上下文嵌入并与竞价拼成每个「买家-物品」对的初始表示 E，再经过一层或多层 Transformer 交互层建模买家与物品间的相互影响，最后由输出层给出分配 g 和支付 p。每个交互层同时融合三种视角——全局平均、按列的 Transformer 和按行的 Transformer——从而在保持置换等变的同时捕捉复杂的交互关系。

zh.text: 论文地址：https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12489
开源代码：https://github.com/zjduan/CITransNet
训练一个规模，迁移到另一个规模
CITransNet 参数量与拍卖规模无关这一性质，带来一个有意思的能力：在某个规模上训练，直接在另一个规模上评测，作者称之为「out-of-setting 泛化」。图2展示了三组这样的实验：把在某个设定上训练好的模型，分别放到买家数或物品数不同的拍卖上运行，并和 Item-wise Myerson 基线比较收益。

zh.caption: 图2 Out-of-setting 泛化结果。模型在一个固定规模上训练，再在买家数或物品数不同的同类拍卖上评测，所有实验的后悔均低于 0.001。(a) 在设定 E（3×10 离散）上训练，评测不同买家数；(b) 在设定 D（2×5 离散）上训练，评测不同物品数；(c) 在设定 G（2×5 连续）上训练，评测不同物品数。蓝线（CITransNet）在大部分未见规模上都稳定高于红线（基线）。

zh.text: 可以看到，即便面对训练时从未出现过的买家数或物品数，CITransNet 依然保持低后悔，并在大多数未见规模上超过基线。对一个需要频繁应对不同参与者数量的线上系统来说，这种「训一次、跨规模用」的性质相当实用。

en.title: From Fixed Auctions to Contextual Ones: CITransNet Learns Better Mechanisms
en.subtitle: ICML 2022 · Peking University and Google propose a permutation-equivariant transformer that folds public context into automated auction design

zh.title: ICML 2022 | 把「上下文」交给 Transformer，让神经网络学出更好的拍卖机制
zh.subtitle: 北京大学与 Google 提出 CITransNet：一个置换等变、可处理变长输入的上下文拍卖设计网络

en.caption: Figure 1. The CITransNet architecture. The network takes a bidding matrix b, bidder-contexts x, and item-contexts y; it embeds the contexts and assembles them with the bids into an initial per-bidder-item representation E, passes this through one or more transformer-based interaction layers that model the mutual influence among bidders and items, and reads out the allocation g and payments p in a final output layer. Each interaction layer sums three views of the data (a global average, a transformer applied along each column, and a transformer applied along each row), which captures rich interactions while keeping the mechanism permutation-equivariant.

en.text: Why context and variable size matter

Classical automated auction design treats each auction as an isolated numerical problem: given a set of bidders' valuations over a set of items, output an allocation and payments. But in real ad auctions, bidders and items are not anonymous. User profiles, advertiser verticals, and product categories are public features that strongly shape what a good mechanism looks like, and ignoring them throws away usable information. At the same time, the number of bidders and slots shifts every round, so a designer whose network is hard-wired to one fixed scale is awkward to deploy. CITransNet targets both problems at once: ingest the context, and accept variable-length input.

zh.caption: 图1 CITransNet 的整体结构。网络接收竞价矩阵 b、买家上下文 x 和物品上下文 y，先把上下文嵌入并与竞价拼成每个「买家-物品」对的初始表示 E，再经过一层或多层 Transformer 交互层建模买家与物品间的相互影响，最后由输出层给出分配 g 和支付 p。每个交互层同时融合三种视角——全局平均、按列的 Transformer 和按行的 Transformer——从而在保持置换等变的同时捕捉复杂的交互关系。

zh.text: 一句话总结与边界

CITransNet 的核心信息很简单：把公开上下文当作一等输入，用一个置换等变的 Transformer 去处理，就能学出接近最优、必要时不对称、且激励相容的拍卖机制；又因为网络规模与买家数、物品数无关，一个训练好的模型可以迁移到未见过的拍卖规模上。需要留意的是，这些结论都建立在合成数据、最大 5×10 的规模上，零后悔是作为软约束逼近而非严格保证，离真实工业级广告系统仍有距离。但作为把上下文特征、不对称机制和跨规模泛化三者统一到一个架构里的尝试，它给「用神经网络设计拍卖」这条路指出了一个务实的方向。

en.subtitle: ICML 2022 · Peking University and Google propose a permutation-equivariant transformer that folds public context into automated auction design

zh.title: ICML 2022 | 把「上下文」交给 Transformer，让神经网络学出更好的拍卖机制
zh.subtitle: 北京大学与 Google 提出 CITransNet：一个置换等变、可处理变长输入的上下文拍卖设计网络

en.caption: Figure 1. The CITransNet architecture. The network takes a bidding matrix b, bidder-contexts x, and item-contexts y; it embeds the contexts and assembles them with the bids into an initial per-bidder-item representation E, passes this through one or more transformer-based interaction layers that model the mutual influence among bidders and items, and reads out the allocation g and payments p in a final output layer. Each interaction layer sums three views of the data (a global average, a transformer applied along each column, and a transformer applied along each row), which captures rich interactions while keeping the mechanism permutation-equivariant.

en.text: Experiments: recover the known optimum, then beat strong baselines

The authors evaluate on nine synthetic contextual-auction settings. Settings A–C are single-item auctions whose optimal mechanism follows analytically from Myerson's 1981 theory and serve as a sanity check; Settings D–I are multi-item auctions up to 5 bidders × 10 items (to the authors' knowledge the largest auction size studied in the deep auction-design literature) with either discrete contexts or continuous ten-dimensional context vectors. Every number is averaged over five runs.

On the single-item settings, CITransNet essentially reproduces the Myerson optimum: in Setting A it earns revenue 0.593 against the analytical optimum of 0.594, with regret below 0.001. Tellingly, the context-free RegretNet and EquivariantNet fall short of the optimum even here, which shows that integrating context is not a nicety but a necessity.

The real test is the multi-item settings, where no analytical solution exists and the only yardstick is a strong baseline. Table 1 compares revenue on three representative settings: E (3×10, discrete), F (5×10, discrete, the largest), and G (2×5, continuous context). Item-wise Myerson applies the single-item Myerson auction independently to each item; CIRegretNet and CIEquivariantNet replace CITransNet's transformer interaction layers with RegretNet's fully-connected layers and EquivariantNet's equivariant layers respectively, while still receiving context.

en.caption: Table 1. Revenue on three representative multi-item settings (higher is better; regret ≤0.003 in all settings). CITransNet achieves the highest revenue in all six multi-item settings; three are shown here. Its margin over Item-wise Myerson reaches about 5.6% on Setting E and about 9.9% on the continuous-context Setting G.

en.text: CITransNet wins on all six multi-item settings; the three above are representative. It consistently beats the strong Item-wise Myerson baseline, and it also beats CIRegretNet and CIEquivariantNet, which receive the same context. Since the only thing separating those three models is the interaction-layer architecture, the comparison pins the gain squarely on the transformer interaction layers.

zh.caption: 图1 CITransNet 的整体结构。网络接收竞价矩阵 b、买家上下文 x 和物品上下文 y，先把上下文嵌入并与竞价拼成每个「买家-物品」对的初始表示 E，再经过一层或多层 Transformer 交互层建模买家与物品间的相互影响，最后由输出层给出分配 g 和支付 p。每个交互层同时融合三种视角——全局平均、按列的 Transformer 和按行的 Transformer——从而在保持置换等变的同时捕捉复杂的交互关系。

zh.text: 实验：先复现已知最优，再赢过强基线
论文在九个合成的上下文拍卖设定上做了评测。其中设定 A–C 是单物品拍卖，最优机制可由 Myerson 1981 年的理论解析给出，用来做「体检」；设定 D–I 是多物品拍卖，规模最大到 5 个买家 × 10 件物品（据作者所知，这是深度拍卖设计文献里考察过的最大规模），上下文既有离散的，也有连续的十维向量。所有数字都是 5 次运行的平均。
在单物品设定上，CITransNet 几乎精确复现了 Myerson 最优：以设定 A 为例，它拿到 0.593 的收益，对应的理论最优是 0.594，后悔值低于 0.001。值得注意的是，不带上下文的 RegretNet 和 EquivariantNet 在这些简单设定上都够不到最优，这直接说明「把上下文整合进来」不是锦上添花，而是必要的。

真正的看点在多物品设定上——这里没有解析解，只能和强基线比。下表对比了几种方法在三个代表性设定上的收益：E（3×10，离散）、F（5×10，离散，最大规模）和 G（2×5，连续上下文）。Item-wise Myerson 是把 Myerson 单物品拍卖逐个物品独立应用得到的强基线；CIRegretNet 和 CIEquivariantNet 则是把 CITransNet 的 Transformer 交互层分别换成 RegretNet 的全连接层和 EquivariantNet 的等变层，但同样吃上下文。

zh.caption: 表1 三个代表性多物品设定下的收益对比（数值越高越好；所有设定中后悔均 ≤0.003）。CITransNet 在全部六个多物品设定中都取得最高收益，此处展示其中三个；在设定 E 上比 Item-wise Myerson 高约 5.6%，在连续上下文的设定 G 上领先约 9.9%。

zh.text: CITransNet 在全部六个多物品设定里都拿到了最高收益，表1里的三个只是代表。它不仅稳定超过 Item-wise Myerson 这个强基线，也超过了同样带上下文的 CIRegretNet 和 CIEquivariantNet。由于这三者唯一的区别就是交互层的结构，这个对比把性能提升干净地归因到了 Transformer 交互层本身。

en.caption: Figure 1. The CITransNet architecture. The network takes a bidding matrix b, bidder-contexts x, and item-contexts y; it embeds the contexts and assembles them with the bids into an initial per-bidder-item representation E, passes this through one or more transformer-based interaction layers that model the mutual influence among bidders and items, and reads out the allocation g and payments p in a final output layer. Each interaction layer sums three views of the data (a global average, a transformer applied along each column, and a transformer applied along each row), which captures rich interactions while keeping the mechanism permutation-equivariant.

en.text: Takeaway and limits

The core message is compact: treat public context as a first-class input and process it with a permutation-equivariant transformer, and you can learn auction mechanisms that are near-optimal, asymmetric when they need to be, and incentive-compatible. Because the network's size is independent of the number of bidders and items, one trained model transfers to auction sizes it never saw. The honest caveats: these results are on synthetic data up to a 5×10 scale, zero regret is approached as a soft constraint rather than strictly guaranteed, and there is still distance to a production-scale industrial ad system. Still, as the first architecture to unite contextual features, asymmetric mechanisms, and out-of-setting generalization, CITransNet points a practical direction for learning auctions with neural networks.
